The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum "Things that were, things that are,and some things that have not yet come to pass."As this article concerns something not yet released, it is subject to major changes. The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum is the working title of an upcoming film produced by Warner Bros. under its New Line Cinema studio and distribution subsidiary. It will be directed by Andy Serkis with Peter Jackson, Fran Walsh, and Philippa Boyens as producers,[2] and was set to be released in 2026,[3] but slipped to December 2027 according to Serkis.[4] In early May 2025, its premiere date was set at December 17, 2027.[1] Contents 1 Cast 2 Crew 3 Plot 4 Development 4.1 Casting 5 Notes 6 Gallery 7 References 8 External links Cast[] Andy Serkis as Gollum[5] Ian McKellen (semi-official)[6][7][8] as Gandalf[9] Elijah Wood (unofficial,[10] despite source claim)[11] as Frodo Baggins[9] Crew[] Director: Andy Serkis Producers: Peter Jackson, Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, Pamela Abdy, Jonathan Cavendish, Mike De Luca, Ken Kamins, Andy Serkis, and David Zaslav Writers: Fran WalshPhilippa BoyensPhoebe GittinsArty Papageorgiou Plot[] The film depicts the titular "hunt for Gollum," prior to the events of The Fellowship of the Ring.[12] During this period, Aragorn, Gandalf, and Sauron are all looking for Gollum. The story is told from Gollum's perspective.[13] Development[] Discussions for another Lord of the Rings film began sometime after the release of The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies.[14] Serkis was brought onboard around November 2023, as Warner Bros. wanted to rejuvenate the Middle-earth IP, starting with a Gollum film.[citation needed] Serkis was asked to direct with Peter Jackson returning to produce.[2][15] It was reported in May 2024, that the film was in early script development involving Walsh and Boyens, along with Phoebe Gittins and Arty Papageorgiou.[2] As of December 2024, Philippa Boyens is working on a script or treatment.[16] Filming is expected to begin early or mid 2026,[17] but likely May 2026 according to Ian McKellen.[9] Andy Serkis and key members of the crew arrived in New Zealand around September 10, 2025.[18] Elijah Wood seems to have read preliminary scripts and has responded extremely positively, while strongly implying his return.[19][11] While he has been seen in New Zealand in late 2025,[20] his most recent film role in Bookworm (2024) was filmed in New Zealand and he could be there just for some related followup.[21] Casting[] The only certain casting is Andy Serkis as Gollum and possibly as Smeagol. At the 2025 For the Love of Fantasy[22] in London, Ian McKellen largely confirmed that the Gandalf and Frodo characters would be appearing in the film and hinted it could be the return for himself and Elijah Wood, but did not confirm it.[9] Notes[] As of May, 2024, The Hunt for Gollum is one of two The Lord of the Rings films intended to be produced.[14] The second is another live-action movie that is currently unnamed.[23] Apparently Ian McKellen may have prompted a rumor that The Hunt for Gollum would be two films.[24] Ian McKellen stated in June, 2024, that he had heard Gandalf would appear in the film, but that he had not been approached to reprise the role.[25] In September of the same year, he confirmed that he had been approached to reprise it for both Hunt and other films that would involve Gandalf.[26] In the same month, Serkis hinted that there would be characters returning to the film, stating "there may be characters that we recognize that might be coming back. I’m not going to say who."[12] In September 2024, it was confirmed that Orlando Bloom had spoken to Serkis concerning reprising his role as Legolas. The use of AI to make the character appear younger was discussed.[27] On December 4, 2024, it was reported from an interview excerpt that Philippa Boyens expressed the development team's hope that Viggo Mortensen would return to play Aragorn.[28] She also said she, Andy Serkis, and Peter Jackson had all spoken to him, however his return has not been confirmed as of March 2025. In late 2025, several rumors circulated that the role of Aragorn would be re-cast and Viggo Mortensen would not return.[29][30] Although unconfirmed, Mortensen has definitely not spoken of a return and reports of the producers looking for an actor to potentially replace him are probably true.
